Tumour Size(cm).description: Maximum clinical/pathological diameter of primary tumor in centimeters.
Tumour Size(cm).clinical_significance: Single strongest clinical predictor of axillary nodal involvement in invasive breast carcinoma. Larger tumor volume correlates with increased vascular and lymphatic invasion probability.

Age(years).description: Patient age in completed years at the time of primary diagnosis.
Age(years).clinical_significance: Younger age is an established clinical risk factor for more aggressive breast cancer phenotypes and higher rate of nodal metastasis.

Histological grading.description: Nottingham Histological Grade (Elston-Ellis modification of Scarff-Bloom-Richardson system), Grade 1 to 3.
Histological grading.units: Grade 1 (Well differentiated), Grade 2 (Moderately differentiated), Grade 3 (Poorly differentiated)
Histological grading.clinical_significance: High tumor grade reflects rapid cellular proliferation, marked nuclear pleomorphism, and loss of glandular architecture, predisposing to lymph node metastasis.

ER_encoded.description: Estrogen Receptor nuclear immunohistochemistry status (1 = Positive, 0 = Negative).
ER_encoded.clinical_significance: Estrogen receptor expression governs tumor hormone sensitivity, differentiation status, and systemic therapeutic responsiveness.

HER2_encoded.description: Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2 amplification / overexpression status (1 = Positive, 0 = Negative).
HER2_encoded.clinical_significance: HER2 amplification drives accelerated oncogenic proliferation, invasiveness, and historical predisposition to axillary dissemination.
